evidence.quote: From {{inh|en|enm|thinne}}, {{m|enm|thunne|thünne}}, {{m|enm|thenne}}, from {{inh|en|ang|þynne}}, from {{inh|en|gmw-pro|*þunnī}}, from {{inh|en|gem-pro|*þunnuz|t=thin}} – compare {{m|gem-pro|*þanjaną||to stretch, spread out}} – from {{inh|en|ine-pro|*ténh₂us||thin}}, from {{m|ine-pro|*ten-||to stretch}}. Cognate with {{cog|de|dünn}}, {{cog|nl|dun}}, {{cog|fy|tin}}, {{cog|is|þunnur}}, {{cog|da|tynd}}, {{cog|sv|tunn}}, {{cog|la|tenuis}}, {{cog|ga|tanaí}}, {{cog|cy|tenau}}, {{cog|lv|tievs}}, {{cog|pl|cienki}}, {{cog|ru|тонкий}}, {{cog|sa|तनु|tr=tanú||thin}}, {{cog|fa|تنگ|tr=tang|t=narrow}}. {{doublet|en|tenuis}}. Also related to {{m|en|tenuous}}.

" of comparatively small diameter, narrow; lean, scanty, not dense; fluid, tenuous; weak,… See origin and meaning of thin. from Old English þynne " of comparatively small diameter, narrow; lean, scanty, not dense; fluid, tenuous; weak, poor;" from Proto-Germanic *thunni "thin" (source also of West Frisian ten , Middle Low German dunne , Middle Dutch dunne , Dutch dun , Old High German dunni , German dünn , Old Norse þunnr , Swedish tunn , Danish tynd ).
